about: The one source of Lumen's Content-Security-Policy and security headers. Edit this file, then run `npm run headers:write` (rewrites the policy values in every file listed under `sources`) and commit both. `npm run headers` (CI) fails when any source differs. Why each value is what it is: docs/security/headers.md.

app.why: The editor: index.html and every SPA route. No eval on the page (Graphviz, ruby.wasm and the TypeScript checker run in workers with their own policy); WebAssembly compiles ('wasm-unsafe-eval'). Trusted Types guard every DOM sink (src/lib/trustedTypes.ts). img-src lists only the hosts the app itself loads images from (the map block's OpenStreetMap tiles, GitHub / Google account avatars): there is no https: in img-src or media-src and frame-src is 'self' alone (plan W4.15). Images, video and audio from other sites in notes, and embeds (the embed block, raw <iframe> in notes, Gist), render only after the user allows them, inside /content-frame.html (route content-frame), a same-origin page with its own policy (src/lib/contentFrame.ts); the renderer holds them back until then (src/lib/remoteImages.ts). connect-src has no bare ws: / wss:: the WebSockets the app opens are collaboration signaling (the deployment's own server, and the two public servers when the user opts in: signaling.yjs.dev and y-webrtc-eu.fly.dev, the y-webrtc package's own default since the Heroku servers went away) and the deployment's own collab servers, which the build adds from VITE_WEBRTC_SIGNALING_URL / VITE_YJS_WEBSOCKET_URL (src/build/cspEndpoints.ts). Supabase is not listed: a deployment that uses it sets VITE_SUPABASE_URL, which the build adds the same way. The font hosts stay in connect-src: the service worker's runtime cache fetches the Google Fonts stylesheet and files. webr.r-wasm.org (webR's own CDN) and cdn.jsdelivr.net (its npm package, the fallback) are for one thing only: the webR download the user starts from an R block (plan W1.34; every file checked against the build's checksums), so connect-src, never script-src: the code runs from this origin's cache.

playground-runner.why: Web Playground runner: the page inside the playground block's sandboxed iframe (sandbox="allow-scripts", opaque origin). Runs the user's own project: blob: modules (the linked project files) and eval (Vue's template compiler); framed by the app only. The nonce is the build's one public nonce (vite.config.ts html.cspNonce, shared with the live-js runner), for WebKit, which does not match 'self' in an opaque-origin frame: the entry script carries it, modules it imports inherit it, and the runner sets it on the vendor scripts it adds (src/playground/runner.ts).

livejs-runner.why: live-js runner (T48): hidden sandboxed iframe (opaque origin). The user's code runs in a blob: worker that inherits this policy: eval for the code itself and no network at all. WebKit does not apply script-src to a worker's dynamic import(), so the worker also refuses code containing the word import and removes eval / Function / string timers (open item 11). The fixed public nonce is for WebKit, which does not match 'self' in an opaque-origin frame (vite.config.ts html.cspNonce adds it to the page's script tags).

content-frame.why: Content frame (plan W4.15): the same-origin page in which the app shows what other sites serve into a note, after the user allowed it: an image, a video or audio file, a provider embed (the embed block, a raw <iframe>) or a GitHub Gist. It keeps https: in img-src / media-src and the embed providers in frame-src out of the app's own policy. The app frames it (src/lib/contentFrame.ts) with sandbox="allow-scripts" (opaque origin) for images, media and Gists, and with the providers' old sandbox (allow-same-origin included, which the providers' own frames inherit and need) for embeds; its script (public/content-frame.js) only builds elements from the request in its #fragment — no HTML sink, no network of its own (connect-src 'none'). frame-src: the providers the embed block knows (src/plugins/EmbedBlock.tsx). script-src https://gist.github.com and style-src https://github.githubassets.com: a Gist embed is a script that document.write()s the gist and its stylesheet; the page writes it only in an opaque-origin frame. The nonce is the build's one public nonce, for WebKit, which does not match 'self' in an opaque-origin frame (as the runner pages).

tesseract.why: On-device OCR (T31): the tesseract.js worker and its wasm cores. A dedicated worker takes the policy of its own response; the app's Trusted Types requirement would block the worker's importScripts() of the core. Language models come from raw.githubusercontent.com on first use.

eval-workers.why: Worker scripts that need eval, each served with its own policy so the page allows none: Graphviz (Emscripten embind builds its bindings with new Function), ruby.wasm, the TypeScript checker, and webR's worker under /webr/ (R.js evaluates EM_ASM code of side modules and webr::eval_js with eval). Their network is the app's own origin only.

X-Frame-Options.why: Legacy twin of frame-ancestors 'none'. Nothing frames the app; the two runner pages and the content frame are framed by the app and must not carry it (they use frame-ancestors 'self').

Permissions-Policy.why: Microphone for dictation and voice memos (getUserMedia({ audio: true }) in src/ui/VoiceDictation.tsx). Nothing in the app uses the camera or geolocation, so both are off.

Strict-Transport-Security.why: Only the managed HTTPS hosts send it. The nginx images listen on plain HTTP behind the operator's TLS terminator; includeSubDomains + preload on someone else's domain is their decision.

Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy.why: Only the nginx image (Dockerfile → deploy/nginx.conf; since 13.2 both fly.toml and docker-compose.yml) opts into cross-origin isolation (multi-threaded WebAssembly). See docs/security/headers.md for its cost; keeping it is decision 15.10(7).

Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy.why: Pairs with Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy on the nginx image; every document and worker it serves carries it so nested frames and workers stay loadable.

cloudflare.why: public/_headers: Cloudflare Pages (and Netlify, which applies dist/_headers but cannot detach headers). The build copies it to dist/_headers and adds the deployment's endpoint origins to every connect-src (src/build/cspEndpoints.ts).

vercel.why: deploy/vercel.base.json headers. Vercel reads vercel.ts, which runs at build time with the project's environment: it loads this file and fills the placeholder below with the deployment's endpoint origins (vercel.ts, src/build/cspEndpoints.ts).

csp.why: Placeholder that vercel.ts replaces with the origins of the VITE_*_ENDPOINT workers (and VITE_CSP_CONNECT_EXTRA) the deployment is built with. The app policy also covers the other workers under /assets/ and sw.js there, so their requests to those workers pass too.

netlify.why: public/_headers (Netlify applies the publish directory's _headers, but cannot detach the catch-all rules) plus netlify/edge-functions/runner-headers.ts, which gives the two runner pages and the content frame their own policy and drops the frame denial (plan 13.2, W4.15).

deploy-nginx.why: deploy/nginx.conf + deploy/lumen-runtime-headers.conf: the one nginx image (Dockerfile), built by fly.toml and docker-compose.yml (plan 13.2).

csp.why: Placeholder that the root Dockerfile replaces with the deployment's endpoint origins (dist/.csp-connect-extra, written by the Vite CSP plugin). Without it the header, enforced next to the meta CSP, blocks the configured endpoints.

meta.why: <meta http-equiv> copies in the HTML pages. They also cover the contexts that send no header (Vite dev, Tauri, Capacitor) and are enforced next to the header everywhere else.

csp.why: Ignored in <meta> (CSP3); browsers log an error for it.
Trusted Types are enforced by the production response headers only; the dev server, Tauri and Capacitor webviews have not been verified under them.

tauri.why: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json app.security.csp. Tauri sends it only with .html assets (tauri crate: manager get_asset), so workers keep their own needs; index.html's meta policy is enforced next to it. No open https: in any directive (plan 2.1).

csp.why: A top-level desktop window is never framed (and on Linux Tauri injects the policy as <meta>); Trusted Types as for meta.

Tauri 2's IPC protocol (ipc: on macOS and Linux, http://ipc.localhost on Windows). No https: — connect-src is the app's explicit list, WebSocket hosts included. A desktop build with deployment endpoints (VITE_*_ENDPOINT) passes them at build time: `tauri build --config "$(node scripts/headers.mjs --tauri-config dist/.csp-connect-extra)"` (docs/security/headers.md).

Tauri sends this one policy with every .html asset, /content-frame.html included (it has no per-route header), so the providers that frame embeds need are here. The app's own windows never frame them: the embed block frames /content-frame.html. Images and media from other sites are not loaded on desktop (no https: in img-src / media-src): a per-user approval cannot widen a policy compiled into the app; Gists stay a link (no gist.github.com in script-src).
